request_reconstruction: Select the two named operations; preserve the fixture tolerance; set iterations=1, inspect_definition=true, and each queries list to its first element. The measured IDs have the suffix -fixture-6.
measurement: Python time.perf_counter_ns around each whole oracle process, pinned to CPU 5. Three alternating-order before/after pairs. Includes loading, two surface constructions per operation (warmup and timed), one closest-point query per operation, definition extraction, and JSON output. The operation elapsed_ns field times only construction and is NOT used here.
host_conditions: An exhaustive debug grid test and a release-workspace build were also active; this is a bounded non-isolated workload measurement.

exact_denominator_lower_bound.proof: For each degree-5 U weight trajectory, subdivide its Bernstein controls exactly at 1/2 using Python Fraction of the stored binary64 weights. Every left/right control is at least this positive value. The V Bernstein basis is nonnegative and sums to one.

prototype_timing_note: Single coarse /usr/bin/time process measurements, not repeated kernel benchmarks. All evaluate the same two-query request. The repeated final comparison below is the main evidence.
remaining_limit: Exact mixed-weight closest-point search remains substantially slower than the former floating-point path, even for a rigorously positive denominator. No performance-parity claim.
